AfterObtained.issue: Rollup of guards G1 and N1 per binding rule 4. WarPaint.cs:20-29 upgrades CardsVar(2) randomly chosen upgradable SKILLS in the deck; the port upgrades nothing and consumes no Niche draw.

guards.what: G1 (LIVE): the port implements no pickup effect at all, and the premise behind the stub is false -- after_obtained IS dispatched
guards.issue: MECHANISM: WarPaint.cs:22-27 is `Deck.Cards.Where(c => c != null && c.Type == CardType.Skill && c.IsUpgradable).ToList().StableShuffle(Rng.Niche).Take(Cards.IntValue)` then CardCmd.Upgrade on each -- two random upgraded Skills, permanently. war_paint.py declares only id/name/rarity/has_upon_pickup_effect and its docstring justifies that with 'an out-of-combat deck edit, so this is a no-op stub'. PROMPT.md bug class 12 applied: the premise is false. Relic.after_obtained is a real base hook (sts2_rl/relics/base.py:138-141) and RunState.add_relic calls it on EVERY granted relic (run.py:552); .superpowers/sdd/content-relic-sweeps.md's sweep C lists this unit in the 'out-of-combat pickup effect, stub' family and reports a LIVE dispatch site for it. REACHABILITY (LIVE, executed -- py audit/tools/relic_probes_b17.py upgradestubs): `run.add_relic('war_paint')` changes 0 deck cards, where C# would upgrade 2 Skills (the Ironclad starting deck holds 4 Defends, all Skills and all upgradable, so the effect is available from floor 0). The CONTROL in the same probe is decisive: `run.add_relic('neows_talisman')` upgrades 2 deck cards through the same run.py:552 dispatch (sts2_rl/relics/neows_talisman.py:29-33), so the pipeline is not merely present but already used by a ported relic to do exactly this kind of deck edit. Both sides ported: the relic is Common in the grab bag and the deck is a first-class run object. Observable in RL play (2 permanently upgraded Skills) and in conformance (sts2_rl/conformance/runner.py:618 compares the deck as (id, upgrade_level) pairs). Rule 7: sts2_rl/relics/base.py, run.py, sts2_rl/relics/neows_talisman.py, sts2_rl/conformance/runner.py and .superpowers/sdd/content-relic-sweeps.md are NOT hashed by this record.

guards.what: N1 (LIVE for RNG parity, dormant for RL): `StableShuffle(Rng.Niche)` names an explicit stream and the stub consumes none

Rule 7: audit/records/relic/war_hammer.json and audit/records/relic/whetstone.json are NOT hashed by this record.

guards.what: N2: `c.Type == CardType.Skill && c.IsUpgradable` and the `c != null` null-guard (WarPaint.cs:22)
guards.issue: Recorded so a fix does not lose the filter: the Skill test is what distinguishes this relic from its identical twin Whetstone (Attacks) and from War Hammer (any upgradable card), and `IsUpgradable` is what keeps PROMPT.md bug class 14 from firing -- the sim's Card.upgrade() is a bare `upgrade_level += 1` (sts2_rl/cards/base.py:146-147) with no guard, and 18 ported Curses and 14 Statuses have max_upgrade_level 0. Curses and Statuses are not Skills, so the type filter alone would already exclude them, but a fix that filtered on type and forgot IsUpgradable would still be wrong for any Skill already at its max upgrade level. Carries G1's LIVE label as part of the same missing implementation; no independent observable. Rule 7: sts2_rl/cards/base.py is NOT hashed here.

guards.what: N4: `undo_after_obtained` is absent from this port
guards.rationale: PROMPT.md v6 binding item 3: the helper has no C# counterpart (nothing in the game un-picks a relic), so a port lacking it is not diverging from the source. Operational consequence worth naming: this relic's pickup DOES mutate run state outside run.relics once G1 is fixed (two permanent deck upgrades), so a fix must not add after_obtained without considering the conformance runner's relic swap (sts2_rl/conformance/runner.py:461, :694 call undo_after_obtained on a dropped relic) -- and a card upgrade is not reversible by the clamping pattern PROMPT.md notes for the max-HP family. That is a tooling constraint on the fix, not a fidelity gap. Rule 7: sts2_rl/conformance/runner.py is NOT hashed here.
